source.title: Benchmarking Optimizers for MLPs in Tabular Deep Learning
source.authors: Yu. V. Gorishniy; Ivan Rubachev; Dmitrii Feoktistov; Artem Babenko

record.tranche_reason: Benchmarks optimizer effects on held-out performance in supervised tabular learning, a setting outside the image and language benchmarks named in V4.
record.gate_note: Reports test-set performance comparisons among optimizers. The study does not measure training–test gaps, random-label memorization, width scaling, convolutional inductive bias, large-batch effects, sharpness, or example removal.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares AdamW with momentum SGD on held-out tabular performance. This extends V4 to a new setting with broad joint tuning. The record incorrectly says the adaptive-versus-SGD comparison is unavailable: Figure 1 and Table 10 report it.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is substantially accurate. The authors identify Muon as their strongest overall practical baseline, conditional on tolerating its training overhead. They also highlight AdamW with EMA and Schedule-Free AdamW as strong alternatives for vanilla MLPs; EMA gains are less consistent on stronger architectures.
record.recipe_differences: Optimizer benchmark on supervised tabular tasks; uses early stopping and test-set metrics, rather than the specific image and language comparisons in V4.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer and model family affect reported held-out performance; EMA gains are less consistent on stronger architectures than on plain MLPs.

fits_no_version.finding: Muon improves over AdamW across all five evaluated architecture families, with additional tuning-time overhead.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Muon can improve held-out performance over AdamW in supervised tabular MLPs, with architecture-dependent computational costs.

fits_no_version.finding: AdamW with EMA and Schedule-Free AdamW improve vanilla MLP performance; EMA gains vary across stronger architectures.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight averaging and schedule-free optimization can improve tabular MLP performance, depending on architecture and dataset.

record.problems: The study is purely empirical and limited to MLP-based supervised tabular learning. It does not analyze why the optimizer effects occur. The reported results do not isolate the adaptive-versus-SGD comparison specified by V4.
record.rows_left_out: No rows: aggregate optimizer results do not isolate the comparison named by V4, and the other versions are not tested.

untested.parts: Controlled widening beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.

Image and language benchmarks; learning-rate-and-schedule-only tuning; training-performance comparisons; causal effects of expanding the tuning budget, decoupling weight decay, or switching optimizers. There is no limited-tuning control.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets.
Controlled dropout comparisons; tuning dropout does not isolate its effect.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples.

missing.what: Extract the direct AdamW-versus-momentum-SGD comparison: AdamW wins/ties/loses on 12/3/2 datasets. Retain per-dataset test means and standard deviations for both optimizers, linked to V4. The record's explanation for omitting this comparison is incorrect.

Record the comparison's tuning conditions: independently tuned optimizers, jointly tuned architecture, dropout and weight decay, 100 MLP trials, validation-based early stopping, and evaluation over 10 seeds. SGD momentum and dampening are both fixed at 0.9; no external learning-rate schedule is used.

record.verdict_notes: There are no existing rows to correct. The missing comparisons permit text-based verdicts, but do not establish the limited-tuning component of V4 or a causal benefit from broader tuning. Muon's advantage over AdamW is not itself evidence for V4's adaptive-versus-SGD comparison.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image models.

Image-classification and language benchmarks; adaptive methods versus SGD under limited tuning; broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching optimizers, and word-level language models. The paper compares optimizers on tabular tasks, but its reported aggregate results do not isolate the adaptive-versus-SGD comparison specified by this version.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and removing dropout with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

relationships.condition: Broadly tuned tabular MLPs: the 12 datasets where AdamW beats SGD
relationships.reason: From Figure 1 and Table 10, rather than extracted rows: AdamW wins on 12 of 17 datasets. This supports V4's allowance that adaptive methods can outperform SGD under broader tuning, without establishing that broader tuning caused the reversal.
relationships.display_finding: Reported AdamW results beat SGD on 12 of 17 datasets, but these comparisons remain unverified and do not establish that broader tuning caused the ranking.

relationships.condition: Broadly tuned tabular MLPs: Sberbank Housing, Maps Routing, and Cooking Time
relationships.reason: From Figure 1 and Table 10, rather than extracted rows: these are the three ties between AdamW and SGD under the study's significance rule, consistent with V4's allowance for no adaptive-method penalty under broader tuning.
relationships.display_finding: The study reports three ties under its significance rule, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: Broadly tuned tabular MLPs: Adult and Delivery ETA
relationships.reason: From Table 10, rather than extracted rows: SGD beats AdamW on Adult accuracy (0.8567 versus 0.8542) and Delivery ETA RMSE (0.5490 versus 0.5510). These extend the SGD advantage to two tabular tasks, although they do not test the limited-tuning condition.
relationships.display_finding: Reported SGD results exceed AdamW on Adult accuracy and Delivery ETA RMSE, but these comparisons remain unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
